name: Scalar phases combine
summary: Two global-phase scalar diagrams combine into one, with their phases added.
description:
The diagram consisting of a Z-spider with phase α connected to an X-spider with phase π is the scalar $\sqrt2 e^{i\alpha}$ (see [this rule](../scalar-state-effect/)). This rule expresses diagrammatically that multiplying two such scalars adds their phases: $\sqrt2e^{i\alpha}\cdot\sqrt2e^{i\beta} = \sqrt2e^{i(\alpha+\beta)}\cdot\sqrt2$, where the last factor √2 is a phase-free pair of spiders.

It is one of the scalar lemmas that the book derives from the rules of the ZX-calculus, so that diagrammatic reasoning with scalars does not require translating to numbers.
